title: _bulk_upsert picks a native upsert per dialect and falls back to merge
answers: how are logged model tags written in batches per database
which SQL dialect uses ON CONFLICT versus ON DUPLICATE KEY in the tracking store
why MSSQL logged model tag writes are still slow
where is the batch size for tag upserts
body:
Where: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:_bulk_upsert chooses the write strategy by dialect.
SQLite and PostgreSQL: one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pk columns) DO UPDATE per batch.
MySQL: one INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE per batch.
MSSQL and other dialects: a session.merge() loop, which issues a SELECT per row.
Batching: rows are chunked at batch_size = 100 inside _bulk_upsert to stay under bind-parameter limits.
Callers: SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags (composite key model_id, tag_key) and the SqlSpan writers already using it.
applies: Where batched write logic for SQLAlchemy tracking-store tables lives and which backends get native batching.
says: Saving tags on logged models is noticeably slow when connected to Microsoft SQL Server.
Model tag updates should be written in batches rather than querying row by row.
Tagging many logged models at once takes too long in our tracking database.
Speed up bulk metadata and tag writes for tracking server database backends.
Large batches of model tags should not exceed database parameter binding limits.
search: In mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py, _bulk_upsert selects native batched upserts by dialect, using ON CONFLICT for SQLite and PostgreSQL, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE for MySQL, and falling back to a session.merge() loop for MSSQL and other dialects. Batches are chunked at batch_size = 100 inside _bulk_upsert to stay under bind-parameter limits. It applies to batched tracking-store writes and is called by SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags and SqlSpan writers.
